chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, who said:

I entered upon al-Rida (peace be upon him), and in front of him was a jug; he intended to prepare from it for the prayer. So I approached him to pour water over his hand, but he refused that and said: 'Stop, O Hassan.' So I said to him: 'Why do you forbid me from pouring [water] on your hand? Do you dislike for me to be recompensed?' He said: 'You will be recompensed and I will be burdened.'

So I said to him: 'And how is that?' So he recited: 'Have you not heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saying: Therefore whoever hopes to meet his Lord, so he should do righteous deeds, and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord?'
And here I am performing ablution for the prayer, and it is the worship, so I dislike for anyone to participate with me therein.

key_terms.إِبْرِيقٌ: A jug or ewer used for holding water for ablution
key_terms.فَلْيَعْمَلْ عَمَلًا صالِحاً: So he should do righteous deeds
key_terms.فَمَنْ كانَ يَرْجُوا لِقاءَ رَبِّهِ: Therefore whoever hopes to meet his Lord
key_terms.وَ لا يُشْرِكْ بِعِبادَةِ رَبِّهِ أَحَدا: And not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Rida refuse for someone else to pour water for his ablution?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the Shia concept of *khalasiyya* (purity of worship) in the Imams, illustrating that while servants are rewarded for their service, the Imam bears the spiritual weight of maintaining the absolute sincerity (*ikhlas*) of his own acts of worship. By citing Surah Al-Kahf 18:110, Imam al-Rida emphasizes that ablution is not merely a ritual prerequisite but an integral part of the worship itself, which must remain exclusively his to avoid any form of 'partnership' in the spiritual merit. This reflects the broader theological principle that the Imams' actions are the standard for pure monotheism, distinct from the general reward granted to those who assist them.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Ahmar, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa who said,

I went over to Al-Rezaasws and in front of himasws was a jug intending to prepare from it for the Salaat. So I approached himasws to pour it upon himasws, but heasws refused that and said: ‘No, O Hassan!’ So I said to himasws, ‘Why are youasws forbidding be to pour upon yourasws hand? Do youasws dislike for me to be Recompensed (for it)?’ Heasws said: ‘You will be Recompensed and Iasws would be burdened’.

So I said to himasws, ‘And how can that be?’ So heasws said: ‘Have you not heard Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Saying [18:110] therefore whoever hopes to meet his Lord, so he should do righteous deeds, and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord,
and here Iasws am performing Ablution (Wudhu) for the Salaat, and it is the (act of) worship, therefore Iasws dislike for anyone to participate with me therein’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah has narrated from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ who has said the following:

“Once I visited Ali al-Rida, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. There was a water jug in front of him and he was about to take Wudu’ for Salah (prayer). I went closer to pour water to help him to take Wudu’. He said, ‘Hold it, O Hassan.’ I then asked, ‘Why do you stop me from pouring water so you take Wudu’ and I can receive rewards for it?’ He replied, ‘You will receive rewards, but I will be burdened.’

I then asked, ‘How can that happen?’ He replied, ‘Have you not heard the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, “Those who wish to meet (receive mercy from) their Lord should do good deeds and not allow anyone else to share in (their) worshipping their Lord.” [18:110]
I am about to take Wudu’ for Salah (prayer). I do not want anyone to share with me my act of worship.’”
